_comment: Search spaces for Bayesian optimisation (Optuna TPE). Ranges are fixed BEFORE any tuning run and are never edited after seeing student-test or evaluator results.

n_estimators.why: Boosting rounds. Below 100 the default learning rate underfits. The upper bound of 500 is a compute-budget choice (each fit on the 2M-row training table takes about 30 s at 300 rounds), made before any tuning run; learning rate and rounds trade off, so a lower learning rate can still be explored within this cap.

max_depth.why: Tree depth controls interaction order between distance, heading, speed and arc features. Depth 3 is close to additive; depth 10 can memorise individual arcs, so the upper end tests overfitting.

learning_rate.why: Step size shrinkage. Its effect is multiplicative, so it is sampled on a log scale; it trades off against n_estimators.

subsample.why: Row sampling per tree. Candidates from the same GPS point are strongly correlated, so some row subsampling acts as regularisation.

colsample_bytree.why: Feature sampling per tree. Several features (distance, distance rank, distance minus minimum) are correlated; sampling decorrelates trees.

min_child_weight.why: Minimum hessian mass in a leaf. Larger values stop leaves fitting tiny groups of candidates from one trip.

reg_lambda.why: L2 penalty on leaf weights; smooths predicted probabilities, which matters because the HMM consumes them.

gamma.why: Minimum loss reduction to split. 0 is the default; larger values prune splits that barely help.

var_smoothing.why: Variance floor added to every feature. Gaussian NB has no other hyperparameter; heavily skewed features such as distance can make the fitted variances unstable.

cv_macro_f1.why: Candidate-level macro F1 averaged over trip-grouped folds; insensitive to the positive/negative imbalance among candidates.

cv_top1.why: Observation-level Top-1 averaged over folds; matches the map-matching goal but is lenient when several candidates are labelled positive.

cv_log_loss.why: Probability quality, which is what the HMM emission model uses. Chosen as the default objective after the baseline runs showed that macro F1 at a fixed 0.5 threshold is misleading here: each GPS point has ~12 candidates and exactly one positive (candidate positive rate ~7%), and a calibrated Gaussian NB predicted no positives at all (macro F1 0.48) although its log loss improved and its ranking (AUC) was unchanged. Decided before any tuning run, using training-partition CV and student-test baselines only.
